_comment: CANON-09/INV-52 (#2563): per-ID allowlist for catalog `enforcement` strings that name NO file-ish token (.mjs/.ts/.java/.yml/.yaml). Every entry here is reviewed individually — this is NOT a substring/keyword match (that would re-green INV-28's own confirmed defect: a string that merely CONTAINS 'CI' or 'policy'). Adding an ID here is a deliberate claim that the named mechanism is real and the reason is accurate; an unlisted vague enforcement string fails the gate.

INV-01.reason: Generic architectural invariant applied across every governed target language; the concrete tools (madge/go vet/cargo check/pylint) are already named literally in the enforcement string. No single arbiter-owned script exists because the check varies per target language's own toolchain.
INV-01.enforcement: CI (madge / go vet / cargo check / pylint)

INV-02.reason: Same class as INV-01 — tool names (Knip/cargo doc/PMD/unused linters) are literal in the string; enforced by the target project's own per-language CI, not an arbiter script.
INV-02.enforcement: CI (Knip / cargo doc / PMD / unused linters)
